prediction: The list is a plausible choice at sixteen entries when cancellation and contiguous due-prefix expiry dominate; ordered insertion costs linear key comparisons.
The heap should reduce order comparisons for unfavorable insertion order, but arbitrary removal and every expiry repair its index structure.
The wheel should reduce key comparisons for insertion, but empty catch-up has per-tick work and stable simultaneous expiry requires explicit ordering; a burst may dominate its normal case.
All current alternatives reserve the same runtime-selected object representation; no physical memory saving is predicted.
No performance winner is assumed before equal-contract checks and unsanitized measurements. Host measurements do not decide MCU interrupt suitability.
limitations: One fixed capacity and host ABI
